method.rowIdentityValidation: Every log completion matches the same indexed raw report row on engine, route, theme, width, mode and pass/error outcome; all 130 rows match in order.
method.timestampPrecision: Raw log timestamps retain seven fractional digits. Durations use integer microseconds after truncating each timestamp to six fractional digits, matching Python datetime.fromisoformat. This records the already reported six-decimal-second derivation; it is not additional timing precision.
method.groupFormula: sum(durationMicroseconds for each row selected by category) / 1000000

categoryDefinitions.passingNormal: raw row pass == true and mode == normal
categoryDefinitions.passingOther: raw row pass == true and mode != normal
categoryDefinitions.failedNoJs: raw row pass == false; all ten are mode no-js

method.intervalScope: Stdout completion intervals include setup, execution, teardown, checkpoint serialization and logging. The first interval also includes initial collector/browser setup after command start. They are historical inter-row wall intervals, not isolated function CPU timings.
method.crashCleanupFormula: Per failed row: raw lifecycle context-close.elapsedMs minus page-crash.elapsedMs; round each to six decimal milliseconds using decimal half-even and sum. Raw IEEE-derived event values are retained alongside the calculation.
method.crashCleanupScope: The crash-to-context-close interval bounds post-crash observation, attempted failure capture/state and teardown together. Screenshot and state work are not separately timestamped. The raw failure lifecycle includes later teardown events; it contains no dropped events.
method.navigationFormula: truncate_us(first logged navigation pass) - truncate_us(last scenario completion)

navigation.remainingIntervalMeaning: Unfinished post-first-navigation work until cancellation; it is not a completed second navigation measurement.

All measurements describe this exact source, Color artifact, runner and log. Historical intervals are not a lower or upper bound on a future passing GTK lease and do not establish that the unchanged 45-minute protected-main serial controller can or cannot fit a future corrected run.

Giving the ten failed row intervals zero duration would remove 234.299069 historical seconds; the remaining 120 historical passing row intervals still total 964.504745 seconds. This is a generous historical subtraction, not a supported future performance forecast or permission to skip no-js rows.

Measured crash-to-context-close cleanup totals 89.471256 milliseconds, about 89.47 ms; the roughly 20-25 second failed row intervals mostly precede crash observation. The retained evidence does not support blaming them on 30-second failure screenshots/state waits.

A supported no-js correction requires a fresh complete GTK measurement at its exact source/tree/artifact/target identity, including all 130 scenarios, all four navigation rows and all 13 analytics rows, before claiming corrected lease duration or a passing full gate.
